title: Yang–Mills and the Mass Gap over Finite Holographic Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The lattice determinations of $m(0^{++})/\sig$ for $\SU(3)$: the $r_0$ route with two inputs, $3.70(6)=5.73(9)\times0.6462(30)$ and $3.63(10)=4.21(11)/1.160(6)$, and the direct continuum extrapolation $3.405(21)$ with the first scalar excitation $5.855(41)$, a spread of $9\,\%$; $T_c/\sig=0.6462(30)$ ($\SU(3)$), $0.7091(36)$ ($\SU(2)$); the $r_0$ masses of $0^{++}$, $2^{++}$, $0^{-+}$ and $0^{++*}$.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The colour factors measured at LEP: $C_A=2.89\pm0.21$ and $C_F=1.30\pm0.09$ from the four-jet angular correlations, $C_A/C_F=2.22\pm0.11$ from the jet multiplicities.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The strong coupling at two laboratory scales, $\alpha_s(M_Z)=0.1180(9)$ and $\alpha_s(m_\tau)=0.312(15)$, with the thresholds $M_Z$, $m_b$ and $m_\tau$.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The one-loop coefficient $b_0=\frac{11}{3}C_A-\frac43T_Fn_f$ and, for the confrontation of P2 only, the two-loop coefficient $b_1=102-\frac{38}{3}n_f$. The paper imports the forms; the structure of the one-loop coefficient as a sum over the field species is the import A12, and its two rationals are the frame's (C13).

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The laboratory instances: the Subjects $\p=13$, $173$, $1549$ with their Carriers $\Om=233$, $30089$, $2408561$, and the sweep over the $21$ shells $\p=4\kap+1$ below $200$; the colour frame's full centre needs $\p\equiv5\pmod{12}$, which the Subject $173$ and $12$ of the $21$ shells satisfy.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: Four results of the framework: time is the drive (a theorem), mass is winding rate with masslessness as drive-invariance, confinement is the wrap of $\Om$-hard quark residues into exact hadron residues, and the gauge sector has one $\Om$-hard scale.

rows.label: A7
rows.predicate: Wilson's lattice gauge theory: the plaquette action on the hypercubic lattice, its strong-coupling character expansion, and the area law $W(A)=c_3^{A}$ at strong coupling, whose chart reading is the tension $a^{2}\sigma=-\ln c_3$ in lattice units, within the expansion's convergence.

rows.label: A8
rows.predicate: Two results of the interactions paper: the character lift (near the identity the frame's character equals the compact group's, to the stated order, with the lift's parametrisation imported as it stands) and the order $\gcdop(3,q+1)$ of the centre of $\SU(3,\F_q)$.

rows.label: A9
rows.predicate: Steinberg's restriction theorem with the linkage principle: for the finite frame and $a+b+2\le\p$, the invariants of $\mathbf3^{\otimes a}\otimes\bar{\mathbf3}^{\otimes b}$ are the algebraic group's, hence the compact multiplicities (degrees to $8$ for $c_3$, $9$ for $c_8$; every Subject above $11$); the integer multiplicities verified on $\SU(3,\F_2)$ over $\F_4$ to degree four (C9).

rows.label: A10
rows.predicate: Casimir scaling of the string tension at intermediate distance, $\sigma_8/\sigma_3=C_A/C_F=\frac94$, the lattice's observation; a bounding value of the tension parameter of C8.

rows.label: A11
rows.predicate: The $0^{++}$ channel of the strong-coupling expansion for $\SU(3)$: $am=-4\ln u-3u+9u^{2}-\frac{27}{2}u^{3}-7u^{4}-\frac{297}{2}u^{5}+\frac{858827}{10240}u^{6}+\frac{47641149}{71680}u^{7}$ in $u=c_3$; its coefficients are rationals of the same multiplicities as $c_3$, not recomputed here.

rows.label: A12
rows.predicate: The one-loop coefficient as a sum over the field species of a paramagnetic spin term and a diamagnetic charge term, $b_0=\sum(-1)^{2s}\bigl[(2s)^{2}-\frac13\bigr]T(R)$, one complex scalar, one Weyl fermion and one real vector each counting once. The form of the sum is imported; its two rationals are computed in C13.

blocks.title: The finite theory and its readings

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: A registration of a state, a channel with one singlet, by its frame is a line of the state's space that every frame element maps to itself; the residue is the number of such lines: photon $2$ (the split torus), gluon $0$ (the adjoint), baryon $1$, meson $1$, glueball $1$. Falsifier: a registered state of residue $0$.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: [chart] The chart's scale is read on the drive: a registered scale is a nonzero element $w$ of the Subject, two scales differ by the power $n$ with $\gen^{n}=w_2/w_1$, and the chart's $\ln(\mu_2/\mu_1)$ is read as $n\ln\gen$ within one window of the drive (a wrap adds $(\p-1)\ln\gen$). The registration $\mu\mapsto w$ is the quantum paper's readout, not computed here.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The finite theory is the transfer form of lattice gauge theory on the substrate: the $\SU(3,\Fp)$ connection on the Subject's cells, the drive as the time step, the action in $\Z[\zeta_M]$ with the framed-rational readout. Its chart objects are the weight $e^{-\beta S}$ with real $\beta$, the wrap operator of C8 and the scale of B2.

blocks.title: The registrations, the sub-horizon tower and the tension

The non-split torus has no shell eigenvalue. For every frame of the totality a norm-one element $a+b\sqrt
u$ with $b

rows.label: T04

legend.name: Import
legend.text: A standard result, a framework result, or a measured datum used here without reproof.

legend.name: Definition
legend.text: A naming, a declared dictionary, or a set-up move, carrying no empirical content; a [chart] definition is a declared continuum reading.

legend.name: Realisation
legend.text: States what a physical term denotes on the substrate: constitutive, not interpretive, and carrying its falsifier.

legend.name: Theorem
legend.text: Proved at the statement the source column names, which also lists the rows it rests on; machine-verified in exact arithmetic by the named check and, where a Lean cell is named, proved in the framework's axiom-free core.

legend.name: $\Om$-hard
legend.text: Decided by the totality; not closeable by a bounded observer; read from the chart.

legend.name: Open
legend.text: A hypothesis not yet derived or a task not yet executed; only in blocks Y and T.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.no_shell_eigenvalue
C1.doc: 46:C1, 46:X1 — a norm-one element `a + b√ν` of the extension with `b ≠ 0`, `ν` a nonsquare, has no eigenvalue in the shell: a root `r` of its characteristic polynomial `x² − 2a x + 1` would give `(r − a)² = a² − 1 = ν b²`, so `ν = ((r − a)/b)²`, a square. Hence a non-scalar element of the non-split torus fixes no line of the shell plane, and the torus fixes none: the gluon, the residue `0` of the non-split torus, is never registered alone.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.scalar_of_im_zero
C1.doc: 46:C1 — the two scalars `±1` are the only norm-one elements with `b = 0`: `a² = 1` forces `a = ±1`.

C1.name: FRC.YangMills.split_fixed_lines
C1.doc: 46:C1 — the split torus `diag(g, g⁻¹)` fixes exactly the two coordinate lines of the projective line: a point `[x : y]` is fixed iff `g x · y = x · g⁻¹ y`, i.e. `(g² − 1) x y = 0`, i.e. `x y = 0` since `g² ≠ 1` (the drive is primitive of order `p − 1 > 2`). The photon's two helicities, residue `2`.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.centre_sweep
C2.doc: 46:C2 — the arithmetic of the centre's order formula. Given that the centre of `SU(3, 𝔽_q)` is the norm-one cube roots of unity, `gcd(3, q + 1)` of them (27-fields Proposition su3, imported, not proved here), on every shell of the sweep below `200`, `q ≡ 5 (mod 12)` gives `Z₃` and `q ≡ 1 (mod 12)` the trivial centre, and the admissible residue `q ≡ 5 (mod 12)` is exactly `q ≡ 1 (mod 4)` (a shell) with `q ≡ 2 (mod 3)` (the triality centre). Kernel-decided over the range, so that no library lemma on `gcd` or `%` (which carry `propext`) enters.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.lab_centres
C2.doc: 46:C2 — the laboratory Subjects: `173 ≡ 5 (mod 12)` has the centre `Z₃`; `13` and `1549`, both `≡ 1 (mod 12)`, have the trivial centre.

C2.name: FRC.YangMills.admissible_sweep
C2.doc: 46:C2 — of the `21` shells `p = 4κ + 1` below `200`, the `12` with `p ≡ 5 (mod 12)` carry the centre `Z₃` and the other `9` do not.

C3.name: FRC.YangMills.glueball_singlet
C3.doc: 46:C3, 46:X2 — by the singlet multiplicities of the tensor powers of the colour triplet (the hadrons theme's `moment6`, six times the multiplicity, computed as the constant term of the Weyl character polynomial — exact integers): the adjoint has no invariant (`E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`, the gluon's residue `0`), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛` has one singlet (`E[χ³] = 1`, the baryon), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` one (`E[χχ̄] = 1`, the meson), and `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟠` one (`E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = E[χ²χ̄²] − 2E[χχ̄] + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, the glueball): photon `2`, gluon `0`, baryon `1`, meson `1`, glueball `1`.

C4.name: FRC.YangMills.casimirs
C4.doc: 46:C4, 46:X4, 46:P1 — the Casimirs of the colour frame with denominators cleared: `2N C_F = N² − 1` gives `6 C_F = 8` (`C_F = 4/3`), `C_A = N = 3`, `2 T_F = 1`, and `C_A / C_F = 2N² / (N² − 1)` gives `8 (C_A/C_F) = 18` (`9/4`).

C5.name: FRC.YangMills.b0_pos
C5.doc: 46:C5 — `b₀ > 0` for every `n_f ≤ 16` (the sign the chart calls asymptotic freedom, for the matter content `n_f ≤ 16`).

C5.name: FRC.YangMills.b0_neg
C5.doc: 46:C5 — `b₀ < 0` for every `n_f` from `17` to `200` (a bounded sweep, kernel-decided).

C6.name: FRC.YangMills.drive_exponent
C6.doc: 46:C6 — every winding rate `w ≠ 0` is one power of the drive: `w = gⁿ` for some `n < p − 1` (the discrete logarithm of 26-pnp, `FrameCore.eq_pow_of_ne_zero`).

C6.name: FRC.YangMills.drive_exponent_add
C6.doc: 46:C6 — the exponent of a product is the sum of the exponents, read modulo `p − 1`.

C7.name: FRC.YangMills.moments
C7.doc: 46:C7 — the moment lists `(ex k)` and `(exc k)` for `k < 8`, from the Pieri multiplicities.

C7.name: FRC.YangMills.c3_fractions
C7.doc: 46:C7 — the eight fractions of `c₃` modulo `β⁸`, from the multiplicities of `moments`.

C7.name: FRC.YangMills.c3_readback
C7.doc: 46:C7 — the residue of every fraction of `c3_fractions` is the series' coefficient on the shell (`c3Check`): on the three laboratory Subjects and on the `20` shells `13 ≤ p < 200`; the shell `5` is blind to the coefficients of `β⁶` and `β⁷`, whose denominators it divides.

C7.name: FRC.YangMills.c2_lab
C7.doc: 46:C7 — `SU(2)`'s `β/4 − β³/96 + β⁵/1536` against `2T`'s `β/4 − β³/96 + β⁵/1280` on the three laboratory Subjects: the same coefficients through `β³`, the first difference at `β⁵`.

C9.name: FRC.YangMills.adjoint_two_sheets
C9.doc: 46:C9 — the two multiplicity identities of the adjoint wrap: the `β¹` coefficient of the adjoint plaquette coefficient vanishes (`E[χ²χ̄] + E[χχ̄²] − E[χ] − E[χ̄] = 0`, no singlet in `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟛` or `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟛̄`), and `4 E[(χχ̄ − 1)(Re χ)²] = 2` (`E[χ³χ̄] + 2E[χ²χ̄²] + E[χχ̄³] − E[χ²] − 2E[χχ̄] − E[χ̄²] = 2`), so `c₈ = β²/288 + …`, the square of `c₃`'s `β/18` up to the factor `9/8`: the adjoint wrap is two fundamental wraps. Stated on the sixfold multiplicities `moment6`.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.spin_traces
C13.doc: 46:C13 — the spin term `(2s)² = −2 Tr(J₁₂²)`: `4` on the vector, `1` on the Weyl spinor (`−Tr((iσ₃)²) = 2`, the generator doubled), `0` on the scalar, with `i = 5, 80, 88` the square roots of `−1` on `13`, `173`, `1549`.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.faulhaber_third
C13.doc: 46:C13 — the Faulhaber identity `3 Σ_{k<N} (N − 2k − 1)² = N (N² − 1)` for every `N < 400` in the integers: the leading coefficient `1/3` is the chart's `∫₀¹ (1 − 2x)² dx`, the lower term `−1/(3N²)` is what the chart discards.

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.faulhaber_residues

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.complete_cycle_vanishes

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.hughes_nielsen_sum

C13.name: FRC.YangMills.faulhaber_third_all
C13.doc: 46:C13 — `YangMillsML.faulhaber_third_all`: the Faulhaber identity `3 Σ_{k<N} (N − 2k − 1)² = N (N² − 1)` for every `N`; the core proves it for `N < 400` and as residues on the shell `173`.

X1.name: FRC.YangMills.no_shell_eigenvalue
X1.doc: 46:C1, 46:X1 — a norm-one element `a + b√ν` of the extension with `b ≠ 0`, `ν` a nonsquare, has no eigenvalue in the shell: a root `r` of its characteristic polynomial `x² − 2a x + 1` would give `(r − a)² = a² − 1 = ν b²`, so `ν = ((r − a)/b)²`, a square. Hence a non-scalar element of the non-split torus fixes no line of the shell plane, and the torus fixes none: the gluon, the residue `0` of the non-split torus, is never registered alone.

X1.name: FRC.YangMills.adjoint_no_invariant
X1.doc: 46:X1 — the adjoint has no invariant: `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` has one singlet (the trace) and the adjoint `𝟠` is its complement, `E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`; with `no_shell_eigenvalue` (the torus fixes no line) no registration singles a gluon out.

X2.name: FRC.YangMills.residue_series_pieri
X2.doc: 46:X2 — one invariant line each: baryon `E[χ³] = 1`, meson `E[χχ̄] = 1`, glueball `E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, by the Pieri multiplicities.

X2.name: FRC.YangMills.glueball_singlet
X2.doc: 46:C3, 46:X2 — by the singlet multiplicities of the tensor powers of the colour triplet (the hadrons theme's `moment6`, six times the multiplicity, computed as the constant term of the Weyl character polynomial — exact integers): the adjoint has no invariant (`E[χχ̄] − 1 = 0`, the gluon's residue `0`), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛` has one singlet (`E[χ³] = 1`, the baryon), `𝟛 ⊗ 𝟛̄` one (`E[χχ̄] = 1`, the meson), and `𝟠 ⊗ 𝟠` one (`E[(χχ̄ − 1)²] = E[χ²χ̄²] − 2E[χχ̄] + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1`, the glueball): photon `2`, gluon `0`, baryon `1`, meson `1`, glueball `1`.
